prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the foreground layout of two side-by-side curved playground tunnel openings (bright white, roughly 0.4 to 1.0 m from the camera wearer) separated by a central vertical post, with two children positioned about 1.0 to 1.5 m apart. On the lower left at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 m distance, a child sits facing right with an outstretched arm touching the inner tunnel wall within their reach, and across frames 1 to 5 their head and back shift left until partly occluded by the left frame border. On the lower right within arm's reach of the camera wearer (roughly 0.5 to 1.0 m away and slightly below eye level), a second child facing away toward the outdoor opening rises from a low crouch at the bottom edge in frame 1 to a more upright posture inside the right chute by frame 5, with both children's lower bodies truncated by the bottom frame edge. This map clearly reveals the 3D silhouette and extended arm of the left child inside the dark tunnel shadow—which is hard to see in the RGB strip—as well as the continuous forward-and-upward depth transition of the right child. However, it is unreliable for the outdoor scene viewed through the right arch and above the tunnels, collapsing the grass, picnic table, trees, and distant buildings (5 to over 20 m away) into a single flat, pitch-black plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only the nearer child on the lower right (labelled 'person', about 0.5 to 1.0 m in front of and below the camera wearer, within arm's reach) across frames 2 to 5, along with two small distant regions visible through the right tunnel opening in frame 4 labelled 'car'. The right-side child's mask grows taller and shifts slightly right from frame 2 to frame 5 as they rise from the bottom edge of the view while facing away from the camera wearer into the slide entrance. While the map highlights a distant vehicle beyond the park lawn in frame 4 (over 20 m away) that is tiny and easy to miss in the RGB image, it offers no spatial layout for the foreground playground structure, which remains entirely unsegmented black background. Furthermore, the map is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the crouched right-side child in frame 1, fails to detect the shadowed child sitting 1.0 to 1.5 m away in the left tunnel across all five frames, and misclassifies the dark park picnic table (roughly 6 to 8 m away through the arch in frame 4) as a 'car'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map fails to detect the actual skeletons or hands of either the shadowed child on the left (1.0 to 1.5 m away, facing right with their arm reaching the tunnel wall) or the nearer child on the right (0.5 to 1.0 m away, within arm's reach, facing away and rising across the 5 frames). Instead, frames 1, 4, and 5 are entirely black, and frames 2 and 3 display only a single erroneous yellow body skeleton near the bottom center of the image. In those two frames, the pose estimator misinterprets the straight blue vertical support post between the two tunnels (about 0.5 to 0.8 m in front of the camera wearer) as a tilted upper torso and places a cluster of false head keypoints on the oval cutouts and bolts of the left tunnel wall below. Consequently, this map adds no valid spatial information over the RGB strip and is completely unreliable due to heavy lower-body occlusion at the bottom frame edge, dark shadows on the left child, and the rear crouched angle of the right child.
